recommended_approach:
Use a Mantaflow LIQUID (FLIP) workflow where you stabilize and control the pour/splash behavior primarily via liquid particle resampling/coverage controls and liquid diffusion properties:
- First tune **Liquid Domain ▸ Liquid** particle coverage/resampling so the stream and splashes keep volume and don’t “leak” or artificially grow: adjust **Particle Radius** (in grid-cell units) when you see undesired volume loss/gain; increase radius if liquid disappears, decrease if too much liquid is produced. Use **Sampling** to sample more particles (at the cost of computation), and use **Randomness** to bias inflow toward laminar (lower randomness) vs more turbulent (higher randomness). Constrain particle counts with **Particles Maximum/Minimum** per cell.
- Then set the fluid’s physical feel in **Liquid Domain ▸ Liquid ▸ Diffusion**: choose/modify a preset and set **Viscosity** in kinematic units (m²/s) using the Base/Exponent scientific-notation UI (example values are provided for water).
- For the “ruby glow / scattering” look (render-side), Cycles’ Principled BSDF **Subsurface** options document that **Random Walk** is best for thin/curved *closed meshes* (and warns that holes/overlaps cause issues), and that radius is RGB-mapped; this is relevant if you choose to approximate scattering with SSS on the liquid mesh rather than purely volumetric shading.

liquid_domain_particle_radius.doc_guidance: Increase when liquid appears to leak/disappear; decrease when too much liquid is being produced (volume gain).

liquid_domain_sampling.doc_guidance: Higher values sample more particles; particle resampling happens at every simulation step (compute cost increases).

liquid_domain_randomness.doc_guidance: 0.0 yields uniform sampling inside grid cells; higher values add more random particle positions in inflow regions (useful for laminar vs turbulent inflow control).

liquid_domain_particles_maximum.doc_guidance: Upper threshold for resampling; helps estimate total particle counts along with grid resolution.

liquid_domain_particles_minimum.doc_guidance: Ensures at least a certain amount of particles per cell.

diffusion_viscosity_water_example.doc_context: Example conversion given for water at ~20°C (dynamic viscosity 1.002 cP; density ~1000 kg/m^3).

options_from_docs: Christensen-Burley (faster/less accurate, may resolve noise faster)
Random Walk (Cycles-only, accurate for thin/curved objects; best for closed meshes)

principled_subsurface_radius_mapping.doc_guidance: Subsurface Radius uses separate RGB channel distances (X/Y/Z mapped to R/G/B) to shape color-dependent scattering distances.

warnings: Liquid particle resampling occurs at every simulation step; increasing Sampling/particle thresholds can raise bake cost substantially.
If the liquid appears to lose volume (disappear/leak), the docs explicitly recommend increasing Particle Radius; if it gains too much volume, decrease Particle Radius.
Cycles Principled Subsurface: Random Walk works best for closed meshes; overlapping faces or holes can cause problems.
alternative_approaches: Use Diffusion panel presets as a starting point, then adjust viscosity from there (docs note a preset menu can be enabled/disabled in the Diffusion panel header).
For render-time scattering, consider Christensen-Burley subsurface if Random Walk is too noisy at your sample budget (docs note Christensen-Burley can resolve noise faster in some situations).
